description: The 'My life' journal: a first-person life story that names people by relationship and never invents a feeling. Every part is a whole sentence American speakers said about their own lives in public-domain federal transcripts (NASA and U.S. House oral histories, congressional hearing testimony, the Congressional Record), counted also against the Library of Congress WPA life histories, 1936 to 1940. The facts are slots from the person's own records. No part names a feeling. Each group names the journal row (kindPrefix) and field it fills; a sentence that names one particular relative is left out, since the journal says whichever relative the record names.

slots.from: The employer a relative left for the one they hold now, as the reader says it: Rasmussen Manufacturing.
slots.school: A school, from the school record.
slots.employer: An employer, from the job record.
slots.other: A person, by name, from the records.
slots.relation: How the writer is related to someone, with the possessive, from the family record.
slots.place: A town, from the household or move record.
slots.wage: An hourly wage, from the pay record.
slots.times: How many times, counted from contact records.
slots.office: An office, from the candidate filing record.
slots.age: An age, computed from the birth record.
slots.law: A law or ordinance, as its record names it.
slots.name: A person, by name, from the records.
slots.whose: A person's name with 's, from the records.
slots.votes: A vote margin, from the results record.
slots.filing_office: Where the person filed, from the filing record (the clerk, the registrar or the board of elections).
slots.named: A relative by relation and given name ("my daughter Jane"), or a person by name, from the family record.
slots.job: A job title with its article ("a county clerk"), from the job record.
slots.span: How long something lasted, in months as people say it, from the dates on its record.
slots.next: The employer someone went to next, from the record of their next job.
slots.topic: What a law no bill enacted is about, from its own record ("electricity and the grid").
slots.signatures: How many signed a recall petition, from the count's record.
slots.required: How many signatures the law required, from the count's record.
slots.fewer: How many fewer signed after the official heard the petitioners out, from the count's before and after.
slots.election: The day of the election a filing is for, as people say a date, from the filing record.
slots.valid: How many signatures on the petition the clerk counted as good, from the petition check record.
slots.needed: How many good signatures the petition needed, from the petition record.
slots.doors: How many doors a volunteer knocked in an evening, from the volunteer-shift record.
slots.held: How long a job lasted, in months as people say it, from the job record's dates.
slots.lost_employer: The employer a lost job was with, from the job record that ended (said only after a job lost, never after a death).
slots.last_employer: The employer who let the person go before a stretch out of work, from that job's record.
slots.paid_more_than: What the job before paid an hour, said only when this one paid more.
slots.paid_less_than: What the job before paid an hour, said only when this one paid less.
slots.moved_from: The place a person moved from, from the moves engine's record of the move.
slots.moved_with: The children born before a move who came with the person, by relation and name, from the family records.
slots.age_then: The person's age on the day of the event, from the birth record and the event's day.
slots.firstborn: The name of the person's first child, from the family record.
slots.together: How long a couple has been together, from the day their partnership's record names, to the day told.
slots.death_age: The age of a person who died, from their birth record and the day of the death.
slots.after_illness: What the death record's topic says the person had been, in plain words.
slots.school_for: How long the person had been at a school, from the school's attendance record.
slots.body: The body a relative's seat belongs to, as the reader says it: the Nelson City Council.
slots.workplace: Where a relative who holds an office also works, as the reader says it: Michael's Market.
slots.count: How many, counted from the records (employers in a working life).
slots.work: The kinds of work a working life was in, from its employers' records ("kitchens and stores").
slots.to: What a person wants done on a question, as a verb phrase after 'to' (question-names.json `to`), from the views engine's stance record.
slots.about: A question as a noun phrase (question-names.json `about`), from the views engine's stance record.
slots.attendees: How many came to a town hall, from its row.
slots.questions: How many questions were asked at a town hall, from its row.
slots.outlet: A news outlet, from its organization's record.
slots.wage_from: The hourly pay of the first job in a run, from its pay record.
slots.wage_to: The hourly pay of the last job in a run, from its pay record.
slots.out_span: How long a person was out of work in all, summed from the work records.
slots.bill: The bill a law moved, from the price rule's good ("electric bill").
slots.amount: About how much a month a bill moved, from the price engine's record.
slots.effects: What laws did to the person's bills, joined from their records.
slots.lean: Which way a view moved ("more liberal"), from the views engine's record of what moved it.
slots.their: A person's possessive pronoun ("his", "her", "their"), from their recorded gender.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.

secondRun.note: Moves added on the second run (a day, a law taking effect, a funeral, voting, results, filing, campaigning, taking office) were mined against the rebuilt corpus and merged into the first run's parts.
